correctness.rationale: If \(W\) meets at least two parts, the induced graph on \(W\) is connected, so a Steiner \(W\)-tree already exists on exactly \(W\); no minimum tree can contain extra vertices, and the Steiner interval is \(W\). If \(W\) lies in one part and has at least two vertices, every minimum Steiner tree uses exactly one outside center, and varying that center makes the interval \(W\cup(V\setminus V_i)\), which equals all vertices exactly when \(W=V_i\). Singletons cannot be Steiner. These cases give the enumerator and inclusion-minimal lower/upper values. Independent brute-force interval rechecks on several small multipartite profiles agreed with the theorem.
